description: A copy of ALM's Pip Slope Mk2: a digital attack-and-decay envelope with a variable curve and three ways of repeating itself

params.text: Sets the attack time, shortest at the bottom of its travel and longest at the top; it comes up in the middle
Sets the decay time, shortest at the bottom of its travel and longest at the top; it comes up in the middle
Bends the curve of both stages, with one shape below the middle of its travel and its mirror image above; it comes up in the middle

Chooses how the envelope repeats: one shot at the bottom of its travel, then a band that repeats with the level halving, then a band of four to ten shortening repeats, and an endless loop near the top

inputs.text: Starts the envelope from zero whenever the voltage rises past 3V
Starts the envelope on a rise past 3V and then holds it at the top of the attack for as long as the voltage stays above 3V, letting the decay run once it falls
Lengthens the attack, adding to the knob; the top of the chosen voltage range adds about three quarters of the knob's own range, and negative voltage does nothing
Lengthens the decay, adding to the knob; the top of the chosen voltage range adds about three quarters of the knob's own range, and negative voltage does nothing

outputs.text: A pulse at the top of the chosen voltage range, 100 samples long, at the end of every envelope
The envelope, from 0V to the top of the chosen voltage range; the menu here offers 10V or 5V where the hardware offers 8V or 5V

notes: the module is monophonic: every jack reads or writes one channel.
nothing happens until something triggers it. Patch a rising voltage above 3V into Trig or Gate, or turn the Loop control past about a quarter of its travel so that the envelope drives itself.
one lamp follows the envelope level; a second lights while the Loop control is in its endless band.
menu: Voltage Range: 10V, 5V — sets how high the Slope Out and the End of Slope pulse reach, and the voltage the two CV inputs treat as a full sweep
